A person who pays attention to the people and not just the systems.
A technical developer who only works on ETL transformation scripts.
An external vendor who sells data management tools to the company.
A member of the legal team who drafts data sharing agreements.
A junior analyst responsible for manual metadata harvesting.
A database administrator who manages user authentication tokens.

question: In the context of the Guiding Coalition, what is 'Position Power'?
options: The ability to type SQL queries faster than other employees.
Ensuring enough key players (main line managers) are on board so progress can't be easily blocked.
The physical office location of the senior data management executive.
The total headcount of the IT department relative to the business.
The number of years an individual has been with the organization.
The level of encryption applied to an administrator's account.
The authority to select the specific hardware vendor for servers.

question: Which of the following is a characteristic of 'Group Think' to be avoided in a Guiding Coalition?
options: Encouraging brainstorming and the use of the scientific method.
Individuals going along with a proposal even when they have reservations about it.
Actively searching for outside knowledge to challenge internal assumptions.
Requiring leaders to speak last during critical decision-making meetings.
Developing multiple alternative solutions before choosing a final path.
Conducting a thorough stakeholder analysis prior to the first meeting.
Mapping project goals directly to organizational strategic objectives.

question: Effective communication of the change vision should strive to keep the message:
options: Highly technical and jargon-heavy to ensure it sounds authoritative.
Simple, by stripping out complex sentences and internal vocabulary.
Encrypted so that it can only be read by authorized stakeholders.
Hidden from the general workforce until the final implementation.
Identical to the marketing messages used for external customers.
Focused exclusively on the specific software version being deployed.
Long and detailed to cover every possible technical scenario.

question: What strategy is suggested for dealing with unavoidable 'inconsistencies' during a change project?
options: Ignoring the question or reacting defensively to 'shoot the messenger'.
Engaging with the question and providing a simple, clear, and honest explanation.
Deleting all records of the inconsistency from the project logs.
Terminating the employees who identified the inconsistency.
Creating a complex technical workaround that hides the problem.
Delaying the project until the inconsistency can be removed entirely.
Replacing the current vision statement with one that matches the error.

question: In the Gleicher formula, why must the product of (D x V x F) be 'greater than' Resistance (R)?
options: To ensure the project budget is utilized effectively.
To ensure the change is enticing enough to overcome the forces of the status quo.
To prove the technical architecture is superior to legacy systems.
To meet the requirements of the annual marketing plan.
To justify the purchase of more expensive hardware servers.
To satisfy the reporting needs of external regulatory bodies.
To increase the speed of real-time network transmissions.

question: According to Bridges, when is a change actually 'complete'?
options: When the project budget has been fully spent.
When the new state is established and comfortable.
Immediately after the 'Ending' phase is announced.
When the first short-term win is celebrated by the team.
When the old systems are physically removed from the data center.
After the first 30 days of the 'Neutral Zone'.
When the executive sponsor signs the final project report.

question: A communication plan for data management value should primarily target:
options: The junior IT staff members who perform daily database backups.
The highest possible influencers, usually executives who fund the program.
External competitors to demonstrate the organization's superior strategy.
The facility managers who maintain the physical office space.
Former employees who have left the organization recently.
Social media influencers who might talk about the company's brand.
Only the users who have identified major data quality errors.
